title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problemStatement: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

examples.explanation: The longest substring without repeating characters is "abc", with a length of 3.
The longest substring without repeating characters is "b", with a length of 1.
The longest substring without repeating characters is "wke", with a length of 3. Note that "pwke" is a subsequence, not a substring.

approaches.name: Brute Force (O(N^2))
algorithm: Use a nested loop structure: Outer loop (i) iterates through all possible start positions, and the Inner loop (j) iterates through all possible end positions (j >= i).
For each substring s[i...j], use a Hash Set to track characters encountered.
As the inner loop advances (j++), check if s[j] is already in the set. If it is, a repetition is found, so break the inner loop and move to the next starting position (i+1).
If s[j] is unique, add it to the set and update `maxLength = max(maxLength, j - i + 1)`.

approaches.name: Optimal Approach: Sliding Window with Hash Map
algorithm: Use a Hash Map (or Array) to store characters and their last seen index: `char -> index`.
Iterate the `right` pointer from 0 to N-1, expanding the window.
For each character `s[right]`, check if it exists in the Map.
If `s[right]` is already in the map, it means a repetition occurred. We must move the `left` pointer.

Update `left = max(left, map[s[right]] + 1)`. Using `max` ensures that `left` only moves forward, avoiding shrinking the window backward if the repeated character was already outside the current window.
Update the index of the current character in the map: `map[s[right]] = right`.
